inconsistencies: #36628 and #36608 are the same private-broadcast rewrite; #36608 is #36628 plus package relay and a CLI tool. Review #36628 first, and treat the outcome as a single direction decision.

That rewrite deletes the in-node private broadcast implementation that #34322, #36477, #36607, #34533, #36330, #34271 and #36566 all extend. Until the direction is settled, review effort on those seven may be wasted; #36477 → #36607 is itself a dependency (the guard needs retained finished-broadcast records).

#34533 and #36330 fix the same leak (wallet rebroadcast under -privatebroadcast) with opposite approaches: route rebroadcasts privately vs. suppress resubmission entirely. They must not both merge as written; #36607 is a broader guard over the same pathway.
#36506 depends on #36437 and subsumes it; review #36437 first, then #36506 for the remaining holes.
#36486 fixes the txid==wtxid ForgetTxHash hole that #36506 also fixes via typed forgetting in TxRequestTracker. Decide in #36506 whether #36486 is still needed.
#36787 is justified almost entirely by #35558 (its author states standalone propagation impact is minimal); review the two together, #36787 first.
Chain #36919 → #36920 → #36933 (BIP332) must be reviewed in that order; only #36919 is independently mergeable.
#35591 is an explicit DO-NOT-MERGE Erlay integration branch; its components are being split into separate PRs that are not in this list, so review attention belongs on those once filed.

Overlapping net_processing surgery: #34824, #35502, #35522, #35561, #35040 and #30988 all rewrite the same files; #35522 was surfaced by review of #34824. Sequencing matters even though it does not change priority.
result.notes: Private broadcast dominates the top of this category: seven PRs touch it and two of them propose replacing the subsystem wholesale. The single highest-value reviewer action is settling that design question, which is why #36628/#36608 sit in P1 alongside the concrete DoS and relay-liveness fixes. The second cluster is 1p1c/orphan relay (#36015, #36437, #36506, #36486, #36328), where importance ordering follows the dependency chain. Refactors were normalised to P3 across the board: #30988 was the only one sitting at P2 while comparable structural work (#34824, #35040, #35561) sat at P3.
